newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth to sell more non-core assets in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth to sell more non-core assets in 1997.

text.p: Woolworth Corp said Wednesday that "significant" year-over-year improvement in first quarter earnings reflects the continued progress it has made in its corporate-wide rebuilding initiatives, and it will continue the orderly disposition of non-strategic real estate and businesses throughout 1997.
The company reported per-share earnings of $0.01 in the quarter ended April 26 versus a loss of $0.17 in the year-earlier period.
First quarter results included a $2 million charge for the closing of its Foot Locker Hong Kong and Basics operation and a $4 million gain on the sale of real estate.

The company also said that its $285 million capital expenditure program for 1997 continues on target. The program includes investing approximately $65 million for new stores and $75 million for remodels or relocations, primarily in the athletic group, as well as $70 million for new state-of-the-art world-wide information systems.
During the first quarter, Woolworth said it opened 33 stores, closed 129 stores, disposed of 92 stores and remodeled or relocated 60 stores.
